scope.purpose: Design-only assessment of responsibility, selected Tag ownership, publication behavior, and sufficiency of compact intent.
scope.established_intent: The authored commitments in the two assessed sources; no additional product intent supplied.

authority.served_model_note: Exact served-model identity was not exposed.
authority.verification: Hashes of the reference and grammar match their output digests in the installed language-pack manifest.

coverage.conclusion: The compact contract communicates sufficient intent for the requested scope. No material contradiction, ownership conflict, omission, or necessary simplification was established.
responsibility: SearchPanel owns its goal of helping users find records with query (panel.sigil:5), its display promise (panel.sigil:8), and its active-request publication constraint (panel.sigil:11).
SearchService owns finding records matching supplied text (service.sigil:3), and accepting search text and returning matching records (service.sigil:6).
selected_tags: SearchService introduces and owns query and search results at service.sigil:6.
The root-relative import at panel.sigil:1 selects those two provider identities. Eligible prose uses query at panel.sigil:5 and search results at panel.sigil:8 and :11.
These references transfer neither Tag ownership nor Facet ownership. They do not by themselves establish a runtime invocation, network boundary, or dependency architecture.
publication_behavior: The authored constraint at panel.sigil:11 states: Only the active request may publish search results.
Derived consequence: a superseded request cannot publish, including when its response arrives late. Enumerating response orderings is unnecessary to establish this exclusion.
The display promise at panel.sigil:8 and publication constraint at :11 are compatible.
The Decisions Facet at panel.sigil:14 explicitly leaves request cancellation as a possible implementation. Cancellation is not a binding architecture choice.
compactness: Goal and Interface contain the required content. Optional State, Logic, and Cases contracts are not needed merely to make the document longer.
No supplied commitment requires a request identifier scheme, cancellation helper, storage structure, retention duration, or exhaustive ordering examples.
The design establishes publication authority without prescribing its implementation.
omitted_scope: Compiler validation and configured workspace discovery.
Product policies beyond the two supplied sources.

limitations: Read-only behavior was an instruction-only restriction; unrestricted filesystem tools were available. No files were created or modified.
Only the two selected project sources and installed evaluator/understanding authority were used. No evaluation fixtures were read.
No compiler or network was used. This is an advisory design assessment, not a tooling-validation or saturated-coherence claim.
Workspace configuration was outside the authorized read scope. Root-relative resolution uses the caller-supplied source root; configured file inclusion was not verified.
Inputs were assessed in place without captures. Reuse requires checking every assessed input and authority identity, and preserving the source-root mapping.
The contract does not establish display retention while another request is pending. No supplied promise makes that policy a material omission in this assessment.
